scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: a 3-day water streak… before I drank anything
scenes.say: Yep. That's an AI giving me a three-day water streak… before I drank a single glass. Let me explain how we got here.
Three AIs. Five real tasks. And one spreadsheet with answers I hid myself, so nobody gets to bluff.
In this corner, ChatGPT. The famous one. Your uncle uses it. Your boss uses it. Your boss's uncle uses it.
Claude. The polite one. It apologises so much, I'm pretty sure it's Canadian.
And Gemini. Google's one. It has the entire internet at home.
Every round is scored out of ten. Fifty points total. Let's go.
Rules. Same prompt. Fresh chat. No re-runs, no editing. All three on paid plans, default models. If an AI embarrasses itself, it stays in the video. That's the deal.
Round one. The thing everyone actually uses AI for: turning messy notes into an email your boss won't laugh at.
Seven facts. A delayed launch, two bugs, a new date, the budget, and one extra test day. Keep all seven. Add nothing.

scenes.label: ChatGPT
scenes.caption: thought about it… then invented one tiny reason
scenes.say: ChatGPT thought about it… said absolutely nothing… then changed its mind. Solid email. But it added one tiny reason I never gave it. Nobody invited that. Nine.

scenes.label: Claude
scenes.caption: kept 7 facts, said “all five”
scenes.say: Claude said untangling, kept every single fact, then proudly told me it kept all five. There were seven. Even Claude can't count all my problems. Still, nothing missing, nothing invented. Ten.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: 11 seconds. Straight to Gmail.
scenes.say: Gemini didn't even think about it. Eleven seconds, straight into a Gmail draft. Every fact. Ten.
Round one: Claude and Gemini tie. ChatGPT, one point behind.
Round two. Trust me, bro. I asked for three laptops under seventy thousand rupees that a student can buy right now, with sources. And I clicked every single link.
Because AI links are like gym memberships. They look great, until you actually use them.

scenes.label: ChatGPT
scenes.caption: said ₹66k · its own link: ₹78,176
scenes.say: ChatGPT said the ASUS Vivobook was sixty-six thousand. Its own link? Seventy-eight thousand. Over budget. That price is from a parallel universe. Six.

scenes.label: Claude
scenes.caption: MacBook out of stock · Lenovo ₹14k more
scenes.say: Claude's top pick, a MacBook? Out of stock. Everywhere. And the Lenovo was fourteen thousand more than it said. To be fair, Claude did warn me to check the live price, especially for the Lenovo. Seven.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: 3 links · 3 prices · all exact
scenes.say: Gemini. Three laptops. Three links. Three prices. All exactly right. I'm genuinely shocked. Someone write this down. Ten.
The lesson: a confident answer is not a checked answer.
scenes.sub: Confident is not the same as checked

scenes.say: Round three. My favourite.
I made a sales spreadsheet for a small shop, and hid three problems inside it. I know the exact answers, so no bluffing.

scenes.label: ChatGPT
scenes.caption: headphone returns 22.8% · revenue falling · missed the region
scenes.say: ChatGPT found the headphone returns, almost twenty-three percent, and revenue falling every month. Every number checked out. But it missed the region, and the weekends. Five.

scenes.label: Claude
scenes.caption: East sales cut in half. then… stopped.
scenes.say: Claude went straight for the region. East sales, cut in half, with a weekly chart. It even spotted days with zero headphone sales in the East. And then… it just stopped. One insight. Four.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: headphones · decline · weak East · a whole dashboard
scenes.say: Gemini found the headphones, the monthly decline, and that the East region was weak. It even built a whole dashboard. Six.
And the answers? Weekends sell sixty-six percent more. The East dropped fifty-two percent from July to September. And headphones get returned almost a quarter of the time.
The weekend one? Not a single AI found it. Apparently AIs don't get weekends.
Round four. No coding. One prompt. Build me a habit tracker in a single file that remembers my habits after I refresh the page.
Then I ran the exact same test on all three. Add two habits. Tick today. Reload.

scenes.label: ChatGPT
scenes.caption: clean, simple, everything saved
scenes.say: ChatGPT: clean, simple, everything saved. Future days locked. Ten.

scenes.label: Claude
scenes.caption: “haven't clicked through it” · honest
scenes.say: Claude: week navigation, a warning if storage fails, and it honestly told me it checked the code but hadn't clicked through it. Respect. Everything saved. Ten.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: prettiest · 3 habits I never added
scenes.say: Gemini built the prettiest app by far. But it came pre-loaded with three habits I never added, including a three-day water streak.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: complete Wednesday on Monday
scenes.say: And it lets you complete Wednesday… on Monday. Productivity unlocked. Eight.
Engineer's verdict: all three apps actually work. Fine for you. If you want to sell it, get the code reviewed first.
scenes.sub: All three work · review before you sell

scenes.say: Last round. Explain AI agents to a fifteen-year-old, then quiz me, one question at a time. And I'm getting one wrong on purpose.

scenes.label: ChatGPT
scenes.caption: built a whole quiz app
scenes.say: ChatGPT built an entire quiz app. With a score table. Calm down. It caught my wrong answer and explained why. Ten.

scenes.label: Claude
scenes.caption: agent = smart intern · 2 out of 3
scenes.say: Claude used a weekend trip to Jaipur, called an agent a smart intern, and graded me two out of three. Fair. Ten.

scenes.label: Gemini
scenes.caption: “Haha, nice try — there is no D!”
scenes.say: Gemini? I answered D. There was no D. Haha, nice try. There is no D. Caught me. Ten.
All three taught it well, and graded me honestly.
Final scores, out of fifty. ChatGPT… forty. Claude… forty-one. And the winner… Gemini, with forty-four.
The winner gets absolutely nothing. It's software.

But here's what actually matters. Writing an email? Claude or Gemini. Shopping with sources? Gemini, but still click the link. Spreadsheets? None of them found everything, so check the numbers yourself.
A quick app? ChatGPT or Claude. And learning something new? Any of them.
The biggest surprise: three of the smartest AIs in the world, and not one noticed that people shop more on weekends.
So, which AI is best? Honestly, the one you double-check.
